gaps.sentence: As long as the budget ___, we can hire two more staff.
gaps.hint: as long as plus a passive condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' takes the present simple, here in the passive: is approved.

gaps.sentence: If I had known you were coming, I ___ a cake.
gaps.hint: unreal past result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The result of an unreal past condition is 'would have' plus the past participle: would have baked.

gaps.sentence: He wouldn't be so tired today ___ so late last night.
gaps.explanation: Past condition with present result: if + past perfect, would + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ here now, she would know exactly what to do.
gaps.hint: unreal present needs the subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: For unreal present conditions, formal English uses 'were' for all persons: were.

gaps.sentence: I will write down the address in case I ___ it.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution against a possibility and takes the present simple: forget.

gaps.sentence: Unless the strike ___, flights will be grounded all weekend.
gaps.hint: unless plus a present passive verb
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses use the present simple, here in the passive: is called off.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ my umbrella — I am getting soaked!
gaps.hint: present regret about an earlier decision
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a present regret about a past decision: had brought.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.
